definition: A list of one or more case submitter_ids associated with this data.
The submitter_id or id of the core_metadata_collection to which the supplementary file belongs, i.e., a link to a record in the parent node.
A combination of date and time of day in the form [-]CCYY-MM-DDThh:mm:ss[Z|(+|-)hh:mm]
The text term describing the broad category that the supplementary file falls into.
The text term describing the file format of the supplementary file, for example, PDF, XLSX, JPEG, PNG, TSV, etc.
The type of supplementary file, for example, figures, tables, clinical data, notes, publications, summary statistics, etc.
The submitter_id or id of the dataset to which the supplementary file belongs, i.e., a link to a record in the parent node.
Type of error for the data file object.
Free text to expand upon details for this file
The name (or part of a name) of a file (of any type).
The size of the data file (object) in bytes.
The current state of the data file object.

A 128-bit identifier. Depending on the mechanism used to generate it, it is either guaranteed to be different from all other UUIDs/GUIDs generated until 3400 AD or extremely likely to be different. Its relatively small size lends itself well to sorting, ordering, and hashing of all sorts, storing in databases, simple allocation, and ease of programming in general.
The 128-bit hash value expressed as a 32 digit hexadecimal number used as a file's digital fingerprint.
The GUID of the object in the index service.
Unique ID for any specific defined piece of work that is undertaken or attempted to meet a single requirement.
The current state of the object.
A human-readable, unique identifier for a record in the metadata database. It can be used in place of the UUID for identifying or recalling a record (e.g., in data queries or uploads/exports).
The node_id of the node in the data model; the name of the node used in queries and API requests (e.g., "aligned_reads_file" for the "Aligned Reads File" node).
A combination of date and time of day in the form [-]CCYY-MM-DDThh:mm:ss[Z|(+|-)hh:mm]
Version of the submitting theranostics extension, independently of the MIDRC baseline version.
Record curation state, independent of clinical value.
Identifier of the originating source record; use an approved pseudonym when needed.
Source system or data provider.
Names of properties missing from this record; no missing value is encoded as zero.
Reasons corresponding by index to missing_properties.
SHA-256 checksum of the immutable artifact.
Format or standard release, including PETSIRD version where relevant.
Profile used to de-identify file contents and metadata.
PET list-mode, SPECT projection, planar projection, sinogram or other raw acquisition.
PETSIRD release for PET list-mode data, if used; do not assume applicability to all modalities.
Role of this existing MIDRC file object in the theranostics workflow.
